method: MIXED. D1-D3 are three AMH pages, paraphrased, no passage stored: the drug choices and all the doses. S1 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP article 'The unwell returned traveller' (October 2025), quoted verbatim, and is used ONLY for the travel-related differential -- it is not a diarrhoea management article and carries no antidiarrhoeal doses. It is included because AMH's Diarrhoea topic cross-refers to a Traveller's diarrhoea topic that was NOT retrieved, and because S1 carries one warning AMH does not: malaria can present as diarrhoea.

claims.claim: Between 43% and 79% of travellers become unwell while travelling or after returning home because of their travel, and TRAVELLERS' DIARRHOEA is among the most common presentations, alongside febrile illness, respiratory illness and dermatological conditions
claims.source_text: It is estimated that between 43% and 79% of travellers become unwell while they are travelling or after returning home because of their travel. … The result is many different diseases that might have a variety of presentations, the most common of which are febrile illness, respiratory illness, travellers' diarrhoea and dermatological conditions.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, 'The unwell returned traveller', Volume 54 Issue 10, October 2025, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2025/october/the-unwell-returned-traveller, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: If diarrhoea is acute and mild, investigations might not be necessary; if it is ongoing acute or chronic, or the patient is unwell, consider investigations -- AND CULTURES MIGHT NOW BE MORE IMPORTANT GIVEN THE INCREASING AMOUNT OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE IN RETURNING TRAVELLERS
